issues.description: Speech-segment identity is complected with transcript value via a mutable _speaking flag
issues.detail: The stream conflates three concerns: the value (text), the identity of the current speech segment, and the time/transition semantics. A boolean flag mutated across two message-type branches encodes a state machine implicitly. Make the segment an explicit value (segment_id + state) or a small pure transition function over events. Right now an empty committed_transcript that arrives before any partial silently does nothing, and the rules are scattered.

issues.description: Protocol dispatch is an if/elif ladder over stringly-typed message_type instead of data
issues.detail: _process_stream_event hand-rolls dispatch on a string, mixing known events, an explicitly-handled-but-ignored event, an error set, and an unknown fallback. This is the abstraction hiding the data. A dict literal mapping message_type to a pure handler (or a parsed event value) would decompose protocol shape from processing and make the unhandled cases obvious. As written, committed_transcript_with_timestamps is dead code that looks intentional.

issues.description: Query-string construction is place-oriented list mutation instead of a values-to-URL function
issues.detail: _connect_ws builds params by appending to a list across nine conditionals, then joins. This is incidental complexity around what is fundamentally {opts -> dict -> urlencoded}. Build a dict of non-None options and hand it to urllib.parse.urlencode. Smaller, harder to get wrong, and the value (the query map) becomes inspectable and testable without a websocket.

issues.description: STTOptions duplicates the constructor signature, complecting defaults across two places
issues.detail: The dataclass defaults (model_id, audio_format, sample_rate) and the __init__ defaults restate the same facts in two locations, and the NotGivenOr-to-None translation is repeated five times inline. Either let STTOptions be the single source of values and construct it directly, or make a small from_kwargs classmethod. Today, changing a default means editing two files in lockstep, and audio_format on the dataclass is a lie since __init__ always overwrites it.

issues.description: audio_format is derived from sample_rate but stored as if independent
issues.detail: audio_format = f"pcm_{sample_rate}" is computed, stored, and then sent over the wire alongside sample_rate. Two fields, one fact. Either drop audio_format from STTOptions and compute it where needed, or validate sample_rate against STTAudioFormat at the edge. As is, an invalid sample_rate (e.g., 11025) silently produces an invalid pcm_11025 string instead of failing fast.

issues.description: Reconnect loop swallows the cancelled task group's exception with a bare .exception() call
issues.detail: tasks_group.exception() is called for its side effect of marking the exception retrieved, but this discards real errors from send/recv. The time semantics of reconnect are also implicit: _reconnect_event is declared but never set anywhere in this file, so the wait_reconnect branch is dead. Either remove the reconnect machinery or wire it; do not keep an inert identity sitting in the code.

review.summary: The plugin works, but it carries the standard incidental complexity of a streaming WebSocket client written by accretion rather than by decomposition. The speech-segment state machine is complected with transcript values via a single mutable boolean; protocol dispatch is a stringly-typed if/elif ladder that hides the shape of the message protocol; query construction is place-oriented list mutation where a dict-to-urlencode would be smaller and testable; and STTOptions duplicates defaults from __init__, with one field (audio_format) being a function of another (sample_rate). The reconnect scaffolding has an unset event and a swallowed exception, which is the kind of detail you only catch by sitting in the hammock with the time semantics first. None of this is wrong in a way that blocks Scribe v2; all of it is the difference between EASY-NOT-SIMPLE and SIMPLE.
